goal: Stop a wedged postgres.js pool connection (active+ClientRead socket stall) from poisoning the worker pool: bulkhead HealthAlertPoller onto its own dedicated client that self-heals by end+rebuild on withTimeout expiry, and add a slow-cadence PoolWedgeReaperPoller that pg_terminate_backends the wedge signature (active+ClientRead, state_change age > threshold, query begins with our cooperative /* rw-reapable */ marker) on a dedicated, runtime-verified-direct connection that bypasses the Supavisor pooler.
non_goals: Reproducing or eliminating the root-cause driver/socket stall itself — the trigger is a rare stall; the bisect (#490 concurrency, Supavisor server-slots) is opportunistic/time-boxed only, and the fix heals regardless of trigger.
Implementing #477's worker-vs-dashboard pool split or pool-wait observability (separate ticket, blocked by #474). The reaper's dedicated client is wedge-containment, not the pool split.
Moving the whole worker off the Supavisor transaction pooler onto direct/session-mode connections.
Changing any health-check SQL, thresholds, or semantics.
Per-query cancellation via postgres.js .cancel() — rejected: unproven against a socket wedge; client-side destroy+rebuild is the chosen reclaim.
Any change to approval / auto-approval / billing / moderation logic.
user_visible_behavior: A wedged health-check connection self-heals within one poll cycle (<=~30s) instead of permanently starving the pool.
HealthAlertPoller's wedge no longer starves the shared pool / the other ~20 loops — it is bulkheaded onto its own dedicated client.

New PoolWedgeReaperPoller terminates any /* rw-reapable */-marked backend stuck in active+ClientRead beyond the age threshold, emitting a warning-level structured log (and health finding) on each termination.
When the worker cannot obtain a runtime-verified-direct connection, the reaper stays disabled and raises a Sentry warning — no crash, no fallback onto the pooler it is meant to heal.
On ticket close, the HEALTH_ALERT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=86400000 staging mitigation is reverted to the 300000 default.
invariants: The reaper NEVER terminates a backend whose current query does not BEGIN WITH the cooperative marker '/* rw-reapable */' in the current database, and only when also pathologically stuck (active AND wait_event='ClientRead' AND now()-state_change > threshold). The marker is opt-in SCOPE, not authentication (it is forgeable and only RepWorth code injects it today, on the five read-only health-check queries) — so the honest guarantee is 'never an UNMARKED backend', which by construction spares publisher/approval/billing writes.
A per-sweep termination cap (runaway guard) is never exceeded; when candidates exceed the cap the dropped count is logged.

The terminate is a SINGLE statement that revalidates (pid, backend_start) plus the full signature atomically, closing the select/kill TOCTOU and PID-reuse race down to a residual microsecond-scale window inside pg_terminate_backend that is accepted (single-replica worker per ADR 0005; the statement is idempotent if ever scaled).
Best-effort/observability failures in the reaper or the health-client recycle never crash the worker nor flip a completed job to failed (production.md log-and-swallow; crash-net stays intact).
Health checks remain read-only; the reaper's pg_terminate_backend is the only new server-side side effect and runs solely on the reaper's own dedicated connection.

Invariant #15: dedicated postgres clients are created only via the src/lib/db/server owner factory and used only by composition-root pollers registered in worker/index.ts; both dedicated clients (reaper + health) are closed in the worker shutdown path.

The reaper runs only on a connection RUNTIME-VERIFIED as genuinely direct (it sets application_name at connect and confirms it echoes back — Supavisor swallows it to 'Supavisor'); if it cannot get a verified-direct route it DISABLES + ALERTS (Sentry warning), never falling back to the pooler it is meant to heal, so it can heal even during a full-pool outage.
No change to approval/auto-approval/billing/moderation paths; tenant-scope and RLS audits stay green.
edge_cases: Supavisor flattens client application_name to 'Supavisor' server-side -> backend identity uses a cooperative query-comment marker, not app_name (captured as ADR 0007); the same flattening is reused as the reaper's direct-route self-check.
The marker match is anchored to the query PREFIX (LIKE '/* rw-reapable */%'), not a substring, to avoid matching the marker buried in another query's comment/string literal.
query_start may restamp each cycle -> the age filter keys on state_change (continuously-stuck-active), not query_start; the candidate SELECT also returns backend_start for atomic revalidation.
Multiple wedged backends in one sweep -> apply the cap, terminate oldest-first (by state_change/age), log the count dropped by the cap.
No verified-direct URL (DIRECT_URL ?? DATABASE_URL both absent or route resolves to the pooler) -> reaper disabled + Sentry-alerted (fail-safe), never crashed, never pooler-fallback.

healthSql.end() on a wedged connection sends FIN (socket.end, not destroy) so server EOF is PLAUSIBLE not guaranteed -> recycle wraps end({timeout:1}) in try/catch and rebuilds UNCONDITIONALLY; the reaper server-side-kills the marked health backend as the backstop if EOF does not land.
The reaper's own dedicated (direct) connection may fail to connect or itself stall -> bounded op-timeout per sweep, self-recycle, skip the cycle; no crash.
pg_terminate_backend returns false if the pid/tuple already vanished (self-heal/redeploy race) -> tolerate.
Reaper marker also matches the now-bulkheaded health poller's own wedge; the in-process self-heal should win first, but an overlapping terminate is harmless (both kill the same stuck backend).
